source.title: The Dark Side of Trust: Authority Citation-Driven Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
source.authors: Xikang Yang; Xuehai Tang; Ji-Zhong Han; Songlin Hu

record.tranche_reason: The study develops and evaluates a citation-driven jailbreak attack, using the general premise that aligned models can be jailbroken. It does not test the listed fine-tuning, first-token, compliant-prefill, suffix/decoding, localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful-response ASRs for DarkCite, an attack using authoritative citations. These results are recorded as findings outside the listed versions: they do not test the specific fine-tuning or first-token mechanisms, or the listed bypass interventions. Table 1 compares DarkCite with other attacks; only DarkCite outcome rows are included. Section 5.4 and Figure 6 describe citation-carrier results across risk scenarios, but the per-condition values are figure-only and are not extracted. The KL and t-SNE analysis compares cited, non-cited, and with-RAG prompts; it is not aligned-versus-base per-response-position KL. Defense pass rates measure the proposed defenses, not the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: DarkCite is a jailbreak that adds fake authoritative citations to prompts. It involves no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no aligned-versus-base per-position KL (V3), no prefill, suffix or decoding attack (V4), no parameter localization (V5), no test of why safety is shallow (V6), and no deepening training (V7). The study does not use the shallow-alignment finding as a tool. It cites Qi et al. (2310.03693) only as the source of the HEx-PHI dataset, so T6 fits better than the reader's T4. Its Figure 8 KL compares cited, non-cited and with-RAG prompts, not aligned versus base models by response position.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that trust in particular citation types varies by risk category, which they attribute to the distribution of risk topics in pretraining data (Finding 2). They also hypothesize that DarkCite acts as an implicit RAG attack, based on the KL and t-SNE analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an authority-citation jailbreak rather than harmful/benign fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base token-position measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported ASR differs across victim models; the paper also describes variation by citation carrier and risk category, with detailed values shown in Figure 6.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompts with fake authoritative citations raise harmful-response ASR from 0% (DI) to 76% on Llama2-7b, 97% on GPT-3.5, 83% on GPT-4 and 7% on Claude-3 (Table 1, Llama-Guard-3 judge, best of 3 samples).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Authority-citation framing elicits harmful compliance from aligned chat models, with effect strongly model-dependent.

record.problems: The attack evaluation uses three repeated trials per prompt and counts a prompt as successful if any one attempt succeeds. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper describes the harmfulness judge as Llama-Guard-3. Some citation-carrier results are presented in figures without extractable per-condition values; Table 1’s reported columns do not include every victim model named in the setup.
record.rows_left_out: Section 5.2/Table 1 results for other attack methods are not separately extracted because they are comparisons, not tests of the listed versions. Figure 6 citation-carrier-by-risk ASRs are not extracted because the per-condition values are figure-only and not stated in the text. Defense ASRs and Table 3 defense pass rates are omitted because they evaluate defenses rather than the listed versions.

untested.parts: No aligned-versus-base per-token KL by response position.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attack of its own. GCG and AutoDAN appear only as comparison baselines in Table 1.
No weights or ranks localized or ablated.
No test of whether data or the training objective causes shallowness. The pretraining-distribution argument concerns citation trust, not shallowness.

missing.what: Baseline GCG suffix-attack ASRs run by the study: 18% Llama2-7b, 30% GPT-3.5, 4% Claude-3, 10% GPT-4 (3×100 trials). These bear only loosely on V4, are comparison baselines and are not a test of it, so no verdict is given.
Llama-3-8b-instruct DarkCite ASR of 45% with no defense.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation and tranche from uses_without_test/T4 to cites_only/T6: the study neither tests nor relies on the shallow-alignment finding. The row states were recomputed against Direct Instruction rather than PAP. Success counts if any of 3 samples at temperature 0.9 is judged harmful, which inflates ASR. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or refusal/compliance outcome after fine-tuning.
No fine-tuning on ordinary or benign data.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement by response position.
The evaluated attack adds authoritative citations; the study does not test compliant opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No weights or ranks are localized, edited, or ablated for safety behaviour.
No experiment tests whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
No training to deepen safety across response tokens or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
